clue.text: Weapon is a bind in the house

explanation.surface: Someone says a gun is a nuisance to have at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-barrelled siege gun is one sense; the lime-and-sand paste that binds bricks in a building wall is the other.

clue.text: It's the fashion to scold, but be reasonable

parts.note: mode means the current fashion
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold

explanation.surface: Telling someone off is all the rage, but keep calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen extremes and act within sensible limits is to temper oneself.

clue.text: Lets out for the flicks

explanation.surface: Someone frees prisoners so they can go to the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Frees from custody is the verb sense; new films issued to cinemas (flicks) is the noun.

clue.text: Turns aside men coming in to make declarations

indicators.note: coming in says one piece enters inside the other

parts.note: averts means turns away or aside
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone diverts the arriving men to make statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' is the container signal; 'Turns aside' looks like the definition but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An averment is a formal assertion or statement of fact, a legal declaration.

clue.text: Upholder of a lamp or flag

explanation.surface: A pole that carries either a light or a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright pole supporting a light is one sense (a standard lamp); a banner carried in battle is the other.

clue.text: Find that horse

explanation.surface: Locate the animal in question.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down is one sense; a trace horse is an extra animal hitched by straps to help haul a load.

clue.text: There's no container coming up for gas

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: No tank is rising to hold gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns NOTIN round. Niton was the early name for radon.
explanation.definitionFit: Niton was the original name of the radioactive element radon, a noble gas.

clue.text: Fierce spirit among those barracking hordes

indicators.note: among those says the letters sit inside the following word

explanation.surface: Hostile mood among a jeering crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrack is a strong Eastern liquor distilled from coconut sap or rice, a potent alcohol.

clue.text: Hamlet's legal hold-ups

parts.note: Hamlet's 'to be or not to be' speech lists 'the law's delay' among life's woes

explanation.walkthrough: The soliloquy speaks of 'the law's delay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow legal processes are postponements, the hold-ups Hamlet complains of.

clue.text: Sweet but uninspired lot we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: uninspired means dull and a lot is a set, giving dull set

explanation.surface: Something pleasant though the group producing it seems a dreary bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns DULL SET into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes a sound that is soft and pleasing to the ear, a sweet tone.

clue.text: The bishop finds his job beyond words

parts.note: beyond as in past the limit, meaning past
in words means spoken rather than written, that is oral

explanation.surface: A bishop's work is too wonderful to describe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral work is a clergyman's care of his flock, the duty a bishop has to his people.

clue.text: " Him that yon soars on golden wing… The Contemplation " (Milton)

definitions.text: " Him that yon soars on golden wing… The Contemplation " (Milton)

parts.words: Him that yon soars on golden wing… The Contemplation " (Milton
parts.note: a line from Milton's Il Penseroso, with the angel's name left blank before Contemplation

explanation.walkthrough: In Il Penseroso Milton writes of 'The Cherub Contemplation', fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Il Penseroso names contemplation as a winged angel of the second order.

clue.text: It's true, Monsieur, about the estates

parts.note: true means real or genuine
M is the standard abbreviation for the French title Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman agrees with a remark concerning landed property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here; 'the estates' are the three estates of a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is traditionally made up of its estates (lords, clergy, commons), so the whole domain is a kingdom.

clue.text: What a' chase for a chary nude!

indicators.note: for here, in an exclamation of a commotion, invites the letters to be chased about into a new order

explanation.surface: Imagine the uproar pursuing a shy naked person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals the anagram of CHARYNUDE; the whole clue reads as the pursuit of a bashful streaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public outcry raised to pursue a criminal was the old English way of chasing a felon.

clue.text: Where to find the meat in a two-decker sandwich ?

definitions.text: Where to find the meat in a two-decker sandwich ?

parts.words: Where to find the meat in a two-decker sandwich
parts.note: the filling of a sandwich sits in the middle, ... the slices; the short poetic form of that preposition is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the clipped form of 'between', with an apostrophe in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The filling lies between the two slices, and the clipped poetic form of that preposition drops its first syllable.

clue.text: Bony wife with good' French gets colourful award

parts.note: in Genesis Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a rib is a wife made of bone
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A skinny woman with good French wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bony wife' calls back to Eve, formed from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is often a coloured strip of silk worn on the chest, like a medal's band.

clue.text: The lighter man shouldered aside?

parts.note: a lighter is a flat cargo boat, and its operator is also, by the -ee ending, one who is pushed aside

explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a barge; to barge is to shoulder aside, so the word reads as 'one barged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal boatman who works a lighter or flat cargo boat.

clue.text: Old boy catches plane with a spurt for a good thing

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a jet is a plane
a dart is a sudden rush or spurt

explanation.surface: A former pupil catches a flight in a hurry for a fine item.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental item of artistic value is a choice treasure.

clue.text: Key to resolve deadlock ?

parts.note: a master key that opens many locks, a burglar's or locksmith's tool, would beat a lock that is stuck

explanation.definitionFit: A pick-like key filed down to open many different locks is named after a bony frame.

clue.text: Beefeaters take one chance among others

indicators.note: among says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the other chances taken are bets
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: Tower guards gamble once among other wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal. Beefeaters are the Tower of London guards, but here the word means cuts of beef that are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskets are cuts of beef from the breast, meat for eating.

clue.text: Boris gets a change under pressure

indicators.note: a change means the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Boris undergoes a transformation when stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map a line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure is drawn, so it is a pressure contour.

clue.text: What a funny card !

parts.note: a card is both a comic character and a playing card; the funny one in a pack is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: The extra picture card in a pack is also a word for a comedian, a funny fellow or card.

clue.text: I'm not in spirits when aboard the sailing ship

indicators.note: not in says that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
I'm gives the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone feels gloomy on board a sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprits are small spars crossing a fore-and-aft sail diagonally, found on board a sailing boat.

clue.text: Exit the avant-garde ?

explanation.surface: The experimental crowd leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving is one sense; daringly modern and unconventional is the other.

clue.text: Like the intentions of those who prepare for war?

definitions.text: Like the intentions of those who prepare for war?

parts.words: Like the intentions of those who prepare for war
parts.note: the Latin saying 'if you want peace, prepare for war' says war preparation has a gentle aim

explanation.walkthrough: It refers to the Latin maxim si vis pacem, para bellum.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who arm to deter war claim their intentions are friendly and calm, aiming at peace.

clue.text: Turn those for make-up

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist these letters round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Turn those over to apply cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the essential character or spirit of a group, its basic nature.

clue.text: Pinched like 18 ?

explanation.surface: Stolen like a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen is the slang sense; having bones, like the bony frame of 18-down, is the other.

clue.text: The Italian among pussyfoots has quixotic tendencies

indicators.note: among says one piece sits in the midst of the other

parts.note: a pussyfoot was a prohibitionist, after the American campaigner 'Pussyfoot' Johnson; teetotallers are TTs
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian moving among cautious types has a dreamy idealistic streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal. A pussyfoot was a prohibitionist; Don Quixote charged at windmills.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote charged windmills with his lance, so someone given to quixotic attacks jousts at windmills.

clue.text: Glover's got a soft job concealing it

definitions.text: Glover's got a soft job concealing it

parts.words: Glover's got a soft job concealing it
parts.note: the saying of firm rule hidden under gentleness puts it inside a velvet glove, the soft work of the glover

explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'an iron hand in a velvet glove'.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm, harsh control is pictured as a metal fist, hidden in the saying under a velvet glove.

clue.text: Nevertheless, it's quite 24 here in Sussex !

definitions.text: Nevertheless, it's quite 24 here in Sussex !

parts.words: Nevertheless, it's quite 24 here in Sussex
parts.note: a Sussex town with a warlike name is in fact a calm place, the 24-across sense

explanation.walkthrough: Battle is a small town in East Sussex, England, named after the Battle of Hastings fought there in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet market town in East Sussex took its name from the 1066 Hastings fight, a warlike name for a calm spot.

clue.text: Earmark an even score

explanation.surface: Labelling a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something for a purpose is one sense; one set apiece, a level tennis score, is the other.

clue.text: Cuts down on allotments ?

explanation.surface: Someone reduces garden plots.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict supplies sparingly is the verb; fixed periods or shares of work assigned are the noun.
